A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Antidistillation Sampling and contain the complete 21-page paper, including Appendices A–D. Text comparison and visual inspection of equations, figures, and example traces support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original distillation experiments on GSM8K, MATH, and MMLU, alongside loss curves, approximation tests, and supplementary comparisons in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original benchmark experiments, loss analyses, approximation tests, and supplementary results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 3 retain the same proxy-gradient calculation, finite-difference penalty, and adjusted next-token sampling procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, including GSM8K Platinum for testing, MATH, and MMLU for the same reasoning tasks. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Temperature sampling, undistilled-student reference performance, and Appendix A's permutation-sampling baseline remain in the same comparisons. Figure 8 also retains the finite-difference versus JVP comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same model configurations, 70%/30% training-holdout partition, answer-scoring procedure, generation limits, and four-epoch LoRA training protocol.

E4.justification: The permutation control, finite-difference validation, architecture comparisons, training-versus-holdout loss analysis, and Appendix D example traces are all retained without revised evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 reports the same means and 95% confidence intervals over bootstrapped LOWESS fits. No run-count, seed, or statistical-estimation information changes.

E6.justification: Figures 1–10 retain identical plotted content, including result points, curves, and uncertainty bands. Numerical statements in the text and the generated examples and accuracy labels in Appendix D are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions and derivations in Section 3, equations (1)–(13), and Appendix B's relative-error definition are mathematically unchanged. Minor typesetting differences do not alter the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about poisoning distillation while maintaining teacher utility through a tunable sampling trade-off.

C2.justification: Both versions give the same interpretations of cross-model generalization and divergent training/holdout losses, and the same qualifications about computational overhead, numerical precision, and applicability.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain unchanged, including hyperparameters, generation lengths, eight-H100 hardware, software libraries, data processing, and code-access links.

R1.justification: The same 50 references and related-work discussion are retained, with unchanged positioning relative to distillation prevention, watermarking, data poisoning, and controlled decoding.

P1.justification: The displayed author name changes from Yixuan Xu to Yixuan Even Xu, and the arXiv version/date stamp updates. Body wording, headings, and section and appendix order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: There are small typographic spacing and alignment shifts in text and mathematical displays. Figures 1–10 and Appendix D's trace panels retain their content, design, and placement; no visual material is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v4 updates an author's displayed name and makes minor typographic adjustments while retaining the same scientific content and appendices. The method, evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information provide no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
